source_refs.note: Exercise 10.1, Question 19 (book p. 278); the book prints no answers for Exercise 10.1; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
The fraction has the exact shape \(\frac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A\tan B}\), which is \(\tan(A + B)\).
To find: the solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution.
Plan: compress to \(\tan(10x + \frac{\pi}{6}) = 1\), solve with period \(\pi\), divide by 10, count the values, and make sure no tangent in the question is undefined at them.
steps:
Given: \(\frac{\tan(7x + \frac{\pi}{6}) + \tan 3x}{1 - \tan(7x + \frac{\pi}{6})\tan 3x} = 1\).
To find: the solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution.
Method: \(\tan(A + B) = \frac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A\tan B}\) with \(A = 7x + \frac{\pi}{6}\), \(B = 3x\).

Use the addition formula
\[A + B = 10x + \tfrac{\pi}{6}\]
\[\tan\left(10x + \tfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 1\]
Why: the left side is exactly the formula for \(\tan(A + B)\).

Solve for the angle
\[10x + \tfrac{\pi}{6} = \tfrac{\pi}{4} + n\pi\]
Why: \(\tan\theta = 1\) at \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) (quadrant I) and \(\frac{5\pi}{4}\) (quadrant III), which are \(\pi\) apart; the period of tangent is \(\pi\).

Make \(x\) the subject
\[10x = \tfrac{\pi}{4} - \tfrac{\pi}{6} + n\pi = \tfrac{\pi}{12} + n\pi\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{120} + \dfrac{n\pi}{10} = \dfrac{(12n + 1)\pi}{120}\]
Why: \(\frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{3\pi - 2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{12}\); then divide by 10, and \(\frac{n\pi}{10} = \frac{12n\pi}{120}\).

Check that nothing is undefined
\[B = 3x = \tfrac{(12n + 1)\pi}{40}\]
\[A = 7x + \tfrac{\pi}{6} = \tfrac{(84n + 27)\pi}{120}\]
Why: \(\tan\) fails only at odd multiples of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), i.e. \(\frac{20(2k + 1)\pi}{40}\) or \(\frac{60(2k + 1)\pi}{120}\), whose numerators are even. Our numerators \(12n + 1\) and \(84n + 27\) are odd, so both tangents exist. The denominator \(1 - \tan A\tan B\) is not zero either, because \(\tan(A + B) = 1\) is finite. So no root is extraneous.

Check: \(x = \frac{\pi}{120}\)
\[A = \tfrac{7\pi}{120} + \tfrac{20\pi}{120} = \tfrac{27\pi}{120}\]
\[B = \tfrac{3\pi}{120},\quad A + B = \tfrac{30\pi}{120} = \tfrac{\pi}{4}\]
\[\tan\tfrac{\pi}{4} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Why: the left side equals \(\tan(A + B)\).
